subject: correct synthax handling additional nuisance variables and family relationships for mediation test

messages.author: 6c11e19c350aed78
messages.subject: correct synthax handling additional nuisance variables and family relationships for mediation test
parts:
Dear Lavaan community,

I am new to SEM and Lavaan and could not find a good example to doublecheck if my approach and synthax makes any sense.
Therefore I hope somebody can help and have a look. 

The mediation analysis is quite simple, but...
1. there are some nuisance variables to take into account (age, gender and batch effects) to a different agree for the variables.
2. part of the data are within sibling comparisons (always two siblings ), but part are singleton individuals.



The mediation is a simple:
X -> M -> Y

( of note: I have several different instances of M and it is  very likely some of them actuall have the  X -> Y -> M relationship,
Loose intermittant question: should I  therefore also competively test this scenario ?)

M is influenced by two batch effects, age and gender
M ~ BATCH1 + BATCH2 + AGE + GENDER

Y is influenced only by age and gender
Y ~ AGE + GENDER

X is luckily not dependent on any of these things 


My best educated guess was the following: 


##############################

library(lavaan)
llibrary(lavaan.survey)
library(survey)

load("dataset.RData")
# all data is contained in "dataset"


model <- ' 
# direct effect
Y ~ c*X
# mediator
M ~ a*X
Y ~ b*M
# relationship M en Y with nuisance variables
M ~ BATCH1 + BATCH2 + AGE + GENDER
Y ~ AGE + GENDER
# indirect effect (a*b)
mediationeffect := a*b
# total effect
totaleffect := c + (a*b)
#direct effect
direct := c
'

fit <- sem(model, data = dataset, test='bootstrap', bootstrap=1000)

### the "nesting"  factor are the siblings who share the same family ID "IDFAM"
#### from the survey package:
designupdate <- svydesign(ids=~IDFAM, nest=T, probs=~1, data=dataset)

fit.new <- lavaan.survey(lavaan.fit=fit, survey.design=designupdate)
summary(fit.new , fit.measures = TRUE)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: correct synthax handling additional nuisance variables and family relationships for mediation test
parts:
Your syntax looks correct, but lavaan.survey does not pay attention to your request for bootstrapping (see the paper: https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v057i01). It implements different robust adjustments for SEs and chi-squared.  I'm guessing you want a bootstrap CI of the indirect effect?  That's a good idea, but it isn't even fully worked out how to bootstrap nested data, so I would actually recommend the Monte Carlo approach spelled out by Preacher & Selig (2012) and implementable in R using this handy online tool:

http://quantpsy.org/medmc/medmc.htm

Scroll down to the references to download a copy of the Preacher & Selig (2012) article.  It is very simple and flexible.  Essentially, you can leave out the user-defined parameters from the model syntax (:=).  Just extract the robust covariance matrix of the parameters
vcov(fit.new)
as well as the point estimates
coef(fit.new)
Then you can plug in the values of a, b, var(a), var(b), and cov(a,b)  into the online calculator, specify your confidence level (95% by default) and click on "Generate R Code" to print the simulation syntax, which you can copy/paste into your R syntax and run very quickly.

Terry
